# legacy-shared fixture

Legacy (non-SDK) C# projects that share build pieces the way long-lived .NET Framework
solutions do, for `csproj modernize` and the `assemblyinfo` codemod. They build on any OS like
`legacy-csproj`: `Directory.Build.props` gives legacy projects the .NET Framework reference
assemblies as a package.

| File | What it exercises |
|---|---|
| `src/SharedAssemblyInfo.cs` | company, product, and version for the whole solution, linked into every project (NHibernate's `SharedAssemblyInfo.cs`, SmartStoreNET's `AssemblySharedInfo.cs`, Open Live Writer's `GlobalAssemblyInfo.cs`): outside each project's folder and compiled by the others, so it is never edited (OFR4306) |
| `build/Version.targets` | writes `src/GlobalVersionInfo.cs` (git-ignored) before every compilation and adds it to the `Compile` items in a target, as Open Live Writer's `writer.build.targets` does: not a compile item of any project file |
| `src/Layers.Domain/Properties/BuildInfo.cs` | a checked-in version file with an `<auto-generated>` header, which analyzers do not look at |
| `src/*/Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs` | each project's own attributes, which the conversion moves into properties |

| Project | |
|---|---|
| `src/Layers.Domain` | the bottom layer |
| `src/Layers.Data` | references `Layers.Domain` |

Converted, both keep the shared and generated files as they are and set
`GenerateAssembly<Name>Attribute` to `false` for the attributes those declare, so the SDK does
not generate them a second time (CS0579).
